app.name: CCI classification
btn.setup.title:
Project
setup
btn.setup.tip: Coding scope (BIM Ísland, p. 1), building number, storey codes (01, K1, M2), level of development (LOD) and code options. Saved in the project.
btn.params.title: Parameters
btn.params.tip: Adds the CCI parameters under Identity Data on the right categories: from Molio's file (C420) if the studio has it, otherwise from the tool's own file with the same names. Can move a project to Molio's file later without losing values.
btn.classify.title: Classify
btn.classify.tip: Proposes a CCI class for every type and room name. You review and edit before anything is written. With elements selected, only their types are shown.
btn.number.title: Number
btn.number.tip: Type IDs (%QQC001), multi-level type IDs (§B.AD.QQC001) and product IDs (#QQC001). Numbers stay put and are never reused.
btn.locations.title: Locations
btn.locations.tip: Room numbers (B01.01.001) on rooms, and location IDs (+B01.01.001) on doors, windows and equipment from the room they are in.
btn.check.title: Check
btn.check.tip: Reports what is missing, malformed or duplicated, against the project's scope and LOD.
btn.ifc.title: IFC file
btn.ifc.tip: Writes CCI_in_Revit_to_IFC.txt and shows the values for the IFC export's Classification Settings.
msg.need_project: Open a project (not a family) to use the CCI tools.
msg.no_setup:
Project setup has not been run in this model, so the defaults are used (scope: coordinated information exchange, LOD 300).

Continue?
setup.title: CCI - project setup
setup.scope_intro: At the start of a project, the scope of coding is set from the project's needs (BIM Ísland CCI guidelines, p. 1). Only what is ticked is filled in and checked.
setup.scope_other: Other options for specific BIM uses
setup.levels_help: Storey code in room numbers: 01 = 1st floor, K1 = first basement, M2 = mezzanine above the 2nd floor. Mezzanines must be entered by hand. Levels without a code give no room numbers.
setup.roomnum.as_is: Revit Number as it is (1-3 digits)
setup.doorroom.to: The room they open into (To Room)
setup.doorroom.from: The room they open from (From Room)
setup.lod_help: Under Level of Development (REV4), classification code and type ID are required from LOD 300 (openings from LOD 325, plus a unique ID at LOD 400). Elements at a lower LOD are not reported as errors when codes are missing.
setup.write_topnode: Write the domain to CCITopnode, e.g. [L]
setup.write_cls: Fill CCIClassification (read by the IFC export)
setup.copy_inst: Copy type values onto instance parameters
setup.copy_inst_d: Instance values always win over type values. Values someone changed on a single element are left alone; only empty values and old copies are updated.
setup.ifc_d: BIM Ísland points to edition R4 of 26.01.2023. Molio has since moved the material to ikt.molio.dk; check which edition of the shared parameter file you use.
setup.saved_missing_levels:
Settings saved. These levels have no code, so rooms on them get no room number:

{names}
scope.coordination: Coordinated information exchange and link to bill of quantities
scope.systems.d: Classification and function ID on technical equipment (CCIFunctionalID). Function IDs are usually set by the MEP engineers; the tool checks their format.
scope.operations.d: Domain, classification, multi-level type ID and space information (CCITopnode, CCIClassCode, CCIMultiLevelTypeID, CCIMultiLevelLocationID).
scope.product_id.d: A unique ID for each element (CCISingleLevelID, #QQC001).
scope.location_id.d: The room the element is in (CCISingleLevelLocationAtID, +B01.01.001).
set.no_scope: Tick at least one item in the scope.
fmt.class_code: classification must be 1-3 capital letters (X, XX or XXX)
fmt.type_id: type ID in the form %XXXaaa, e.g. %QQC001
fmt.ml_type_id: multi-level type ID in the form §U.VV.XXXbbb, e.g. §B.AD.QQC001
fmt.single_id: product ID in the form #XXXccc, e.g. #QQC001
fmt.functional_id: function ID in the form =Ukk.VVmm.WWnn.XXXppp, e.g. =H01.HD02.EGC001
fmt.location_id: room number in the form Bxx.yy.zzz, e.g. B01.01.001
fmt.location_plus: BIM Ísland recommends not using the + prefix in space information
fmt.level_code: storey code must be 01, K1, M2 etc. ({name}: "{value}")
fmt.classification: CCIClassification in the form [L]XXX or XXX
loc.no_level_code: the level has no code in Project setup
loc.bad_level_code: the level's code in Project setup is not valid (01, K1, M2)
loc.no_room_number: the room number can't be used (1-3 digits)
loc.title: CCI locations
loc.done: Room numbers written on **{rooms}** rooms and locations on **{elements}** elements.
loc.no_room: {n} elements are not in a room with a room number and got no location.
loc.not_point: {n} elements (walls, floors etc.) span several rooms and get no location ID.
loc.not_bound: {n} rooms don't have the CCIMultiLevelLocationID parameter. Run Parameters.
loc.nothing_in_scope: Neither space information (Operations) nor location ID is in the project's scope. Change it in Project setup.
loc.no_level_codes: No storey codes are set. Add them in Project setup (Storeys and rooms tab).

params.title: CCI parameters
params.wrong_type: Not a text parameter in the file
params.missing_help: Parameters missing from the file were not added. Use Molio's file or the tool's own file, which have all of them.
params.conflict_help: A parameter with the same name exists that is not Molio's, or it is type instead of instance (or the other way round). Remove it in Manage > Project Parameters and run again.
params.no_classification: CCIClassification is not in the file. The IFC export uses it as the Classification field name; without it the CCI classification is not exported as an IfcClassificationReference.
classify.title: CCI classification
classify.intro: One row per type (and per room name). Edit the Class column or pick from the table. Source: Guidelines = code from BIM Ísland's/Molio's guides, Suggestion = the tool's suggestion, Studio = a studio rule. Tick Remember to save the classification as a rule. Unticked rows are not written.
classify.intro_sel: Only the types of the selected elements. Edit the Class column where needed. Unticked rows are not written.
classify.fix_codes: Fix these codes first (class 1-3 capital letters, U one letter, VV two):
classify.done:
Classification written on {types} types and {spaces} rooms.

Run Number to update the type IDs.
classify.not_bound: {n} types/rooms are missing CCI parameters and were skipped. Run Parameters.
classify.nothing: No building elements found to classify.
number.title: CCI numbering
number.nothing_in_scope: No IDs are in the project's scope. Change it in Project setup.
number.done: Changed: {type} type IDs, {ml} multi-level type IDs, {single} product IDs.
number.no_class: {n} elements have no classification and got no number. Run Classify.
number.no_parents: {n} elements got no multi-level type ID because the functional system (U) and technical system (VV) are missing. Set them in Classify.
number.not_bound: {n} elements were skipped because CCI parameters are missing. Run Parameters.
check.title: CCI check
check.table_incomplete: The CCI table is marked incomplete. Codes not in it are marked unverified, not wrong.
check.more: ...and {n} more (save as CSV to see all).
check.save_csv: Save the result as a CSV file?
chk.not_bound: The {param} parameter is not on the element
chk.not_applicable: {param} does not apply to this kind of element
chk.override: {param} = "{value}" on the element, "{type_value}" on the type
chk.unknown_class: Class "{value}" is not in the CCI table
chk.unverified_class: "{value}" is not in the table yet (unverified)
rules.no_id: A rule in rules.json has no id
rules.duplicate_id: Two rules in rules.json are called "{id}"
col.name: Name
ifc.pick: Save the CCI property set file for IFC export
ifc.title: CCI in IFC export
ifc.step1_d: File > Export > IFC > Modify Setup > Property Sets tab > Classification Settings. Enter:
ifc.step2_d: On the same tab: tick Export user defined property sets and pick `{path}`. The CCI parameters then end up in the CCI_Administrative property set.
ifc.step3_d: Open the IFC in a viewer (e.g. Solibri or BIMcollab Zoom) and check CCI_Administrative and the classification on a few elements. In particular, check that type values come through when the instance parameter is empty.

params.choose: Where should the CCI parameters come from?
params.opt_tool: The tool's own file (until you have Molio's)
params.opt_save_tool: Save the tool's file (for project partners)
params.is_tool_file: This is CCI-tools' own file, not Molio's. Continue anyway?
params.migrate_ask:
{n} CCI parameters in the project come from another shared parameter file (probably the tool's).

Move them to Molio's file? All values are carried over. Undo works.
params.tool_note: The parameters come from CCI-tools' file: the same names as BIM Ísland's guide, but not the same GUIDs as Molio's file (C420). IFC export and BIM Ísland's IDS checks go by name, so deliveries are the same. When you get Molio's file, this button moves the project over without losing values.
params.other_file_help: These parameters exist in the project from another shared parameter file. The tool uses them as they are.
tx.params_migrate: CCI: move parameters to Molio's file
check.params_tool: The CCI parameters come from CCI-tools' file, not Molio's (C420). Fine for IFC deliveries; move the project over when you get Molio's file (Parameters button).
check.params_mixed: Some CCI parameters come from CCI-tools' file and others from another file. Run Parameters with Molio's file to align them.
